chunks: With this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
His, Exalted is He, saying: “When you rise for salat (prayer)”

What is meant by that, “when you rise for salat (prayer)”? He said: “When you rise from sleep.” I said: “Does sleep invalidate wudu (ablution)?” He said: “Yes, when it overcomes hearing and he does not hear the sound.”

key_terms.إِذَا قُمْتُمْ إِلَى الصَّلَاةِ: the Qur'anic phrase being explained in the narration
key_terms.لَا يَسْمَعُ الصَّوْتَ: he does not hear the sound; the sign mentioned for invalidating sleep
key_terms.مِنَ النَّوْمِ: from sleep; the stated meaning of rising here
key_terms.يَنْقُضُ: invalidates or breaks a state of ritual purity

ai.seo_question: Does sleep invalidate wudu (ablution) according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic phrase “when you rise for salat (prayer)” as referring to rising from sleep. It indicates that sleep invalidates wudu (ablution) when it is deep enough to overcome a person's hearing so that he no longer hears sound.
